questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $z$ and $w$ are two complex numbers, solve the simultaneous equations

$$
3z + w = 9 + 11i
$$

$$
iw - z = -8 - 2i
$$

leaving the answers in the form $a + bi$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Label the equations

$$
3z + w = 9 + 11i, \tag{1}
$$

$$
iw - z = -8 - 2i. \tag{2}
$$

From (1): $w = 9 + 11i - 3z$. Substitute in (2), using $i^2 = -1$:

$$i(9 + 11i - 3z) - z = -8 - 2i \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 9i - 11 - 3iz - z = -8 - 2i.$$

Collect the terms in $z$ on the left:

$$-z(1 + 3i) = -8 - 2i - 9i + 11 = 3 - 11i \quad\Longrightarrow\quad z = \frac{-3 + 11i}{1 + 3i}.$$

Multiply by the conjugate $1 - 3i$ of the denominator:

$$z = \frac{(-3 + 11i)(1 - 3i)}{(1 + 3i)(1 - 3i)} = \frac{-3 + 9i + 11i - 33i^2}{10} = \frac{30 + 20i}{10} = 3 + 2i.$$

Then $w = 9 + 11i - 3(3 + 2i) = 9 + 11i - 9 - 6i = 5i$.

$$\boxed{z = 3 + 2i, \qquad w = 0 + 5i}$$

Check in (2): $i(5i) - (3 + 2i) = -5 - 3 - 2i = -8 - 2i$. Check in (1): $3(3 + 2i) + 5i = 9 + 11i$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Let $\mathbb{N}$ be the set of natural numbers. A relation $R$ is defined on $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ by $(a, b)\,R\,(c, d) \iff \dfrac{d}{b} = \dfrac{c}{a}$. Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Here $\mathbb{N} = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$ (positive integers), so that the quotients $\frac db$ and $\frac ca$ are defined. The relation is on the set $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$ of ordered pairs. Note that $(a, b)\,R\,(c, d) \iff \dfrac db = \dfrac ca \iff ad = bc$.

We must prove that $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

**Reflexive.** Take any $(a, b) \in \mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$. Then $\dfrac{b}{b} = 1 = \dfrac{a}{a}$, which is the statement $(a, b)\,R\,(a, b)$. So $R$ is reflexive.

**Symmetric.** Suppose $(a, b)\,R\,(c, d)$, that is $\dfrac db = \dfrac ca$. Taking reciprocals of both sides (all quantities are non-zero), $\dfrac bd = \dfrac ac$. This is exactly the statement $(c, d)\,R\,(a, b)$: by the definition of $R$ with the roles of the two pairs interchanged, it reads $\dfrac{b}{d} = \dfrac{a}{c}$. So $R$ is symmetric.

**Transitive.** Suppose $(a, b)\,R\,(c, d)$ and $(c, d)\,R\,(e, f)$, that is

$$
\frac db = \frac ca \qquad\text{and}\qquad \frac fd = \frac ec.
$$

Multiply these two equalities member by member:

$$\frac db\cdot\frac fd = \frac ca\cdot\frac ec \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac fb = \frac ea,$$

which says $(a, b)\,R\,(e, f)$. So $R$ is transitive.

Since $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, it is an equivalence relation on $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$. $\blacksquare$

(Equivalently, $(a,b)\,R\,(c,d)$ means $\dfrac ab = \dfrac cd$: two pairs are related when they give the same fraction, and equality of fractions is clearly reflexive, symmetric and transitive. The equivalence classes correspond to the positive rational numbers.)
